notice: Synthetic training knowledge base. Adapt every step to organizational policies; not an authoritative production runbook.

articles.title: Account locked or cannot sign in
articles.summary: Check the exact error, account state, and identity verification procedure before changing access.
steps: Record the error message and whether the issue affects one account or several users.
Verify the requester's identity using your organization's approved procedure before any account changes.
Check account lockout, disablement, password expiration, and recent failed sign-in indicators in the authorized admin console.
Confirm device time and network/domain connectivity when authentication relies on a domain.
Unlock or reset only if authorized, then test sign-in and document the action.
articles.caution: Never bypass identity verification, MFA, or an organization's access controls.

articles.title: Password reset and password expiration
articles.summary: Follow the approved reset workflow and check for stale credentials on other devices.
steps: Confirm the exact account and complete the required identity check.
Check whether a reset is appropriate or if the user can complete self-service recovery.
Use only the organization's authorized reset method; require a new private credential.
Have the user update saved credentials in approved apps and devices.
Confirm access, update the ticket, and avoid recording passwords.
articles.caution: Do not request or store the user's password in a ticket.

articles.title: MFA prompts not arriving
articles.summary: Isolate whether the problem is the app, device, time synchronization, or registered method.
steps: Confirm the expected authentication method and which prompts are missing.
Check the device's time, network connectivity, notification permissions, and authenticator app state.
Ask the user to retry using a permitted backup method if one is already enrolled.
Review authentication logs for denied prompts, failed attempts, or blocked sign-ins.
Escalate account recovery or method re-enrollment under approved policy.
articles.caution: Never approve unexpected prompts or disable MFA merely to bypass an issue.

articles.title: VPN fails to connect
articles.summary: Determine whether the failure involves connectivity, credentials, VPN software, or an outage.
steps: Verify normal internet access before connecting to VPN.
Capture the VPN client name, exact error text, and approximate start time.
Check service status, permitted client version, and device clock.
Confirm the account is authorized and any required MFA is completing successfully.
Retry the documented connection procedure and escalate persistent gateway or certificate errors.
articles.caution: Do not weaken firewall rules or disable endpoint protection to make VPN connect.

articles.title: Wi-Fi connects but internet does not work
articles.summary: Narrow down whether the problem is one device, a wireless network, DNS, or the upstream connection.
steps: Check whether another trusted device on the same Wi-Fi network can reach the internet.
Confirm the device is connected to the intended SSID with a valid IP address.
Check the local gateway and whether name resolution works for approved test sites.
Forget and rejoin the network only when permitted; renew the lease if required.
Escalate suspected access-point, DHCP, or ISP outages with the observed symptoms.
articles.caution: Do not connect a work device to an untrusted hotspot without approval.

articles.title: Printer offline or job stuck
articles.summary: Separate physical printer problems from queue, driver, and connectivity issues.
steps: Check power, error lights, paper supply, and visible jams.
Confirm the selected printer and whether the issue affects one user or several.
Review the printer queue for paused or stuck jobs; clear jobs only with authorization.
Verify the expected printer address and network connectivity.
Use approved driver or spooler troubleshooting and print a test page.
articles.caution: Avoid clearing shared queues without notifying affected users.

articles.title: Windows update or application installation fails
articles.summary: Collect failure details, storage availability, permissions, and deployment policy.
steps: Record the affected app or update, version, exact error, and when it started.
Confirm supported OS version, available disk space, and device management requirements.
Restart when permitted and check whether an approved maintenance window applies.
Review supported update history or installation logs for an error code.
Escalate repeated failures rather than disabling security controls.
articles.caution: Do not install unapproved software or turn off security protection.

articles.title: DNS resolution and website access
articles.summary: Distinguish name lookup failures from general loss of network connectivity.
steps: Confirm the full hostname and whether the issue affects other users.
Test approved websites and basic connectivity to isolate name resolution.
Check that the device received the organization's expected DNS settings.
Inspect resolver errors and compare a known-good device where allowed.
Escalate DNS server, proxy, or filtering changes to network administrators.
articles.caution: Do not replace corporate DNS servers with public resolvers without approval.

articles.title: Computer slow or low on disk space
articles.summary: Inspect resource usage and storage pressure before changing software.
steps: Ask when slowness occurs and whether a restart changes it.
Inspect CPU, memory, and disk usage using authorized monitoring tools.
Check free storage and permitted cleanup targets, including temporary files.
Review recent updates and running apps; avoid stopping essential processes.
Document before-and-after behavior and escalate hardware faults.
articles.caution: Never delete a user's files without permission and a backup plan.

articles.title: Suspicious email or possible phishing
articles.summary: Preserve evidence, reduce interaction, and report possible phishing through established channels.
steps: Tell the user not to click further links, download attachments, or reply.
Record the visible sender, subject, timestamp, and observable signs without forwarding the message casually.
Use the organization's approved phishing-report workflow to preserve the message safely.
If a link was clicked or credentials were entered, immediately follow incident response procedures.
Document the report and alert the security team for analysis.
articles.caution: Do not open suspicious attachments or paste credentials into a report.
